text.p: Rehabilicare Inc expects a turnaround in its international orders in the second half of fiscal 1997.
"This segment was down considerably compared to last year resulting in minimal total revenue growth year-to-year," said president David Kaysen in a statement.

"This trend should reverse dramatically in the second half of fiscal 1997 as our distributor in the United Kingdom finalizes long-term arrangements with Boots Co Plc, the largest chain of pharmacies in the U.K., relative to our BabiTENS product," Kaysen noted.

The executive added, "Our CTDx Electrostimulation System aimed at repetitive stress injuries of the wrist and elbow, is progressing as planned. The abstract results of our double-blind clinical study will be available by the end of October.

"We currently have several significant revenue generating trials under way, and we are billing and being reimbursed for units dispensed out of several large clinics across the country. We expect revenues from this key product to grow as our fiscal year progresses."
Kaysen further noted the company expects further growth in its electrotherapy devices business.
During the September 30 first quarter, Rehabilicare reported earnings of $0.03 per share on sales of $2.3 million.
